To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnetization of Ni2MnGa, NiMn2Ga and Ni3MnGa alloys is determined by the antiferromagnetically coupled Mn atoms in the sublattice of the original Mn atoms and that the chemical ordering has a strong effect on magnetism.

(i) the magnetic interactions between Ni atoms are weak and antiferromagnetic, (ii) the magnetic interactions among Mn atoms on the same sublattice are ferromagnetic and strong, (iii) the magnetic interactions of the Mn atoms on different sublattices are weak and antiferrromagnetic, (iv) the chemical ordering plays a significant role in magnetism, and (v) the magnetization of the off-stoichiometic NiMnGa alloy is determined
the antiferromagnetism between the Mn atoms occupying the original Ni sublattice is the main reason for the decrease of magnetization with Mn content in NiMnGa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetic properties of off-stoichiometic NiMnGa alloy.
the magnetism of off-stoichiometic NiMnGa austenitic alloys.
the magnetic interactions in NiMnGa, which has a wide range of magnetic and structural properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetism of NiMnGa is a complex phenomenon and the magnetization is determined by a subtle interplay of various magnetic interactions.
the magnetization of the off-stoichiometry NiMnGa alloy is determined by the chemical composition and chemical ordering of the alloy.
the magnetization of NiMnGa can be controlled by chemical ordering, chemical substitution, and magnetic field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetism of off-stoichiometry alloys is mainly determined by the magnetic interactions between the chemical species.
the magnetism in off-stoichoimetric NiMnGa can be understood by the competition between ferromagnetic interactions between Mn and Ga, and antiferromagnetic interaction between Mn atoms.
the magnetization of NiMnGa is controlled not only by the Mn concentration but also by the ordering of chemical species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetism of NiMnGa is strongly influenced by chemical ordering and the antiferromagnetism of Mn atoms.
the magnetism of NiMnGa is not simply a function of the chemical composition but also of chemical ordering.
chemical ordering plays an important role in the magnetic properties of NiMnGa and other Heusler alloys.
